Summarise a voxel's values across cells and depth levels

Source: R/summarise_3d.R
summarise_3d.Rd

summarise_3d() computes statistics of every non-NA value of a SpatVoxel, across all its cells and depth levels at once. It is the summarise step of an analysis: the values inside a shape are kept with mask(), and summarise_3d() turns them into a mean, a standard deviation, a range or a median. Compare terra::global(), which summarises each layer, here each depth level, on its own.

Usage

summarise_3d(
  x,
  statistic = "mean",
  weighting = c("volume", "equal"),
  by = NULL,
  bounds = c("midpoint", "top")
)

Arguments

x

A SpatVoxel, typically mask(v, shape) for the values inside a shape, or a list of voxels, one per time step, as as_voxel() gives for a time window. Envelopes have no values, so they aren't accepted; a netCDF file isn't either: describe it with as_proxy() and read one time step with as_voxel().

statistic

One or more of "mean", "sd", "min", "max" and "median". Each becomes a column of the result, in this order.

weighting

"volume" (default) weights each value by the volume of its cell and depth level; "equal" counts each value once. A row whose values all have zero volume, such as a voxel with a single level and no depth edges, or the deepest level under bounds = "top", uses equal weights.

by

NULL (default) gives one row per voxel, so one per time step for a list; "depth" one row per depth level of each voxel, with a depth column. Values from different time steps aren't combined, so a list shows the change from step to step. "time" means the same as NULL, and says in a call on a list that the rows are per time step.

bounds

As in volume(): where the slab edges fall for a voxel that carries no depth edges; used with weighting = "volume" only. Voxels read with as_voxel() from a SpatProxy carry their edges, so bounds isn't used for them.

Value

A data frame with one row per voxel, or per voxel and depth level with by = "depth", in the order of x and then of depth. Columns: time (the voxel's terra::time(), UTC, or NA when it has none), depth (with by = "depth" only, in metres), one column per statistic, and n, the number of values the row is built on, so rows built on too few values can be dropped. A row with no values has NA statistics and n = 0.

Details

With weighting = "volume" (the default), each value is weighted by the volume of its cell and depth level, from volume(x, per_cell = TRUE, per_level = TRUE): cells shrink towards the poles, and depth levels range from a few metres thick to 100 m or more. In a water column with thin warm levels near the surface and thick cold ones below, the volume-weighted mean is colder than the equal-weighted one. weighting = "equal" counts each value once, so sd and median are then stats::sd() and stats::median().

With normalised weights \(w_i\), the weighted standard deviation is the square root of \(\sum w_i (v_i - \bar v)^2 / \sum w_i (1 - w_i)\), the sample standard deviation under equal weights and the same formula as in extract_to_buffer(). The weighted median is the value at which the cumulative weight, over the values sorted from smallest to largest, reaches half the total; when it reaches half exactly, the two values either side are averaged, as stats::median() does. min and max ignore the weights.

See also

mask() to keep the values inside a shape; volume() for the weights; as_voxel() to read one time step of a SpatProxy.

Examples

# One water column sampled at seven depths: thin warm levels near the
# surface and thick cold ones below.
r <- terra::rast(nrows = 1, ncols = 1, xmin = 0, xmax = 1, ymin = 0,
                 ymax = 1, nlyrs = 7, crs = "EPSG:4326")
terra::values(r) <- t(c(20, 19, 18, 17, 16, 8, 4))
v <- as_voxel(r, depths = c(0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 100, 200), varname = "temp")

# The volume-weighted mean is colder: the deep levels stand for more water.
summarise_3d(v, statistic = c("mean", "sd", "min", "max"))
#>   time mean       sd min max n
#> 1 <NA> 10.2 6.271899   4  20 7
summarise_3d(v, statistic = "mean", weighting = "equal")
#>   time     mean n
#> 1 <NA> 14.57143 7

# One row per depth level.
summarise_3d(v, by = "depth")
#>   time depth mean n
#> 1 <NA>     0   20 1
#> 2 <NA>    10   19 1
#> 3 <NA>    20   18 1
#> 4 <NA>    30   17 1
#> 5 <NA>    40   16 1
#> 6 <NA>   100    8 1
#> 7 <NA>   200    4 1

# A list of voxels, one per time step, gives one row per step.
later <- v + 1
terra::time(v) <- rep(as.POSIXct("2020-01-01", tz = "UTC"), 7)
terra::time(later) <- rep(as.POSIXct("2020-01-02", tz = "UTC"), 7)
summarise_3d(list(v, later), statistic = c("mean", "median"))
#>         time mean median n
#> 1 2020-01-01 10.2      8 7
#> 2 2020-01-02 11.2      9 7
